title: kgdiff graph, version 1
description: A graph in kgdiff JSON, as graphToJSON and `kgdiff apply` write it. kgdiff also reads looser JSON (other field names, numeric ids, loose fields as attributes); this schema describes the canonical form. See https://github.com/iiwish/kgdiff/blob/main/docs/formats.md#kgdiff-json

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, for editors.

format.description: Format marker. Optional, together with version; it makes readers recognise the file for certain.

version.description: Version of the format (not of the graph: that is meta.version). Readers reject versions they do not support.

id.description: A node id: an IRI, a CURIE such as GO:0008150, or any non-empty string.

attrs.description: Any other values, by name: strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays and objects.

meta.description: About the graph. Other keys are kept as they are.

version.description: The version of the graph, shown in headers and titles.

source.description: Where the graph came from: a file name, a URL…

predicateLabels.description: Display names of relations, by predicate.

label.description: The display name; defaults to the id. A changed label is a rename.

type.description: A type, or several (class, category, rdf:type).

types.description: The types, as graphToJSON writes them. Use type or types, not both.

deprecated.description: True for an obsolete node that is still present.

replaces.description: Ids of the nodes this one replaces in the other version: a strong merge hint.

replacedBy.description: Ids of the nodes that replace this one: a strong merge hint.

implicit.description: Written by graphToJSON for a node created at an edge end the graph does not describe.

position.description: A pinned layout position. Never part of the diff.

id.description: An explicit edge id, used for identity only when edges are identified by id.

predicate.description: The relation: an IRI, a CURIE or a plain name. Defaults to the empty string.

label.description: Display label of the relation; defaults to a readable form of the predicate.
